# Part II: One Guide, Many Audiences {.unnumbered .part}

London's tourism office has one set of facts and many readers. Visitors want a web page they
can open on a phone. Managers want the numbers at a glance, partners a brief they can forward,
and people who walk in off the street something to take away. The office needs every one of
those versions to say the same thing, and to go on saying it when the visitor counts are
revised.

In this part you play the office's role. You write the guide once, from cited data, and let
Quarto make every version from that one source:

- @sec-markdown turns an empty folder into a web page that changes as you watch, with written
  rules that hold the assistant to cited facts.
- @sec-compute makes the guide compute: the numbers in its sentences and its chart come from
  the data, in three formats at once.
- @sec-audiences serves managers, partners and walk-ins in one step, with three assistants
  working side by side.
- @sec-publish puts the guide on the web, then changes one number and asks you to explain
  everything that changed with it.

The exercises at the end of the part test whether you can do it without the prompts.
